hook: He won the world Scrabble championship in French. He doesn't speak French.
story: His name is Nigel Richards, a quiet New Zealander. His mother taught him Scrabble at twenty-eight, reportedly telling him he'd be no good at it because he couldn't spell. He dominated the English game, five world titles, then went looking for a new challenge. He memorized the entire French dictionary, four hundred thousand words, in nine weeks, without ever speaking the language, and crushed the French competition. Nine years later, he did the same in Spanish.
number: That Spanish title came in 2024, at fifty-seven, in his first-ever Spanish competition. He won twenty-three of twenty-four games, with the first perfect scores ever recorded at the event, which makes him world champion in three languages, and a speaker of exactly one.
closer: He has never explained how. He turns down interviews with a smile, and walks away.

His mother taught him Scrabble at twenty-eight, reportedly telling him he'd be no good at it because he couldn't spell. He dominated the English game, five world titles, then went looking for a new challenge. He memorized the entire French dictionary, four hundred thousand words, in nine weeks, without ever speaking the language, and crushed the French competition. Nine years later, he did the same in Spanish. That Spanish title came in 2024, at fifty-seven, in his first-ever Spanish competition. He won twenty-three of twenty-four games, with the first perfect scores ever recorded at the event, which makes him world champion in three languages, and a speaker of exactly one. He has never explained how. He turns down interviews with a smile, and walks away.
